title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 5, 'Specialization of MD-graphs' (the words 'et généralisation' are struck out of the title), page 15 of the manuscript. An MD-graph (Mumford–Deligne graph) is G = (S, Ã, σ_Ã, I, Î = Ã ⊔ I → S, g: S → ℕ). In modern terms this is a stable graph:
- S is the set of vertices.
- Ã is the set of half-edges carrying the fixed-point-free involution σ_Ã, whose orbits are the edges.
- I is the set of legs (marked points).
- Î → S attaches half-edges and legs to vertices.
- g gives the genus of each vertex.
The numerical type is (g, ν), with g the arithmetic genus and ν = card I.

The preceding page shows that the closure of the stratum M_[G] in the Mumford–Deligne compactification M̂_{g,ν} is the image of M̂_G = ∏_{α∈S} M̂_{g_α, Î_α} modulo Γ = Aut(G). Here Î_α is the set of legs and half-edges at α.

This page derives a combinatorial description of the specializations of G, i.e. the strata lying in the closure of M_[G]. Strata of the product M̂_G are tuples of strata of the factors. A stratum of M̂_{g_α, Î_α} is an isomorphism class of MD-graphs G(α) of type (g_α, Î_α), where Î_α becomes the leg set I(α). Isomorphisms must restrict to the identity on these legs. The trivial one-vertex graph is allowed.

The next page completes the recipe:
- S' = ⊔ S(α).
- Ã' = Ã ⊔ ⊔ Ã(α), with the involution induced by the given ones.
- I' = I.
- The attachment map and the genus function are induced from the G(α).
In words: replace each vertex α by a stable graph with ν_α + μ_α legs and genus g_α, then glue along the old edges. This is exactly graph insertion/substitution: the poset of stable graphs under edge contraction, i.e. the composition in the modular operad {M̄_{g,n}}. The purpose is to describe the stratification 'at infinity' of M̂_{g,ν} and its incidence (specialization) relations, as part of the study of the boundary structure and the Teichmüller tower.
errors: No error on this page itself. On the previous page the map M̂_G/Aut(G) → M̂_{g,ν} is called a closed immersion of multiplicities. In general it is only finite and unramified (a normalization of the stratum closure), because boundary strata self-intersect. Example: the divisor of irreducible nodal curves, image of M̂_{g-1,ν+2}/S_2, is not embedded; a curve with two non-separating nodes has two preimages.
Consistently with that issue, the recipe on this page is many-to-one: different choices of the G(α) up to Aut(G) can yield the same specialized graph G'. The page does not address this here.

ideas.what: MD-graph = combinatorial dual graph of a stable marked curve, given as (vertices, half-edges with involution, legs, attachment map, genus function)
ideas.modern_name: stable graph (dual graph of a stable curve)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Mumford–Deligne stratification 'à l'infini'; the 'MD-graphe' terminology there is unsure

ideas.what: Specializations of a stratum correspond to strata of the product ∏ M̂_{g_α, Î_α}, obtained by replacing each vertex with a stable graph of type (g_α, Î_α) and regluing
ideas.modern_name: graph substitution / edge-contraction poset of stable graphs; modular operad composition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); stratification folklore going back to Deligne–Mumford and Knudsen

ideas.what: Isomorphism classes taken relative to the identity on the legs

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine description of the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n} and its specialization order via vertex substitution. It is standard material and later formalized as modular operads; nothing here is unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Spécialisation [-et généralisation-] des MD-graphes' — the struck word is 'et généralisation', i.e. the original title was 'Spécialisation et généralisation'.
In (38), the map g: S → ℕ appears with 'g' written above/at the arrow, and the gloss Î = Ã ⊔ I is written beneath Î.
'de type numérique (g,ν)' — the parentheses with g,ν are clear in the image.
In the NB, the type of the trivial MD-graph is written '(g_α, ν̂_α)'.
